title: PATH 2 / UNCOND-Λ: Route C dynamical — Dyson-ODE-based dS_{k*}/dtau derivation

derivation.sourceODE: Backward CM flow: d(gamma_k)/dtau = +2 * SUM_{j != k} 1/(gamma_k - gamma_j)
derivation.targetQuantity: S_{k_star}(tau) = SUM_{j not in {k_star, k_star+1}} 1/(d_j * e_j), with d_j = gamma_{k_star+1} - gamma_j and e_j = gamma_{k_star} - gamma_j.
derivation.derivedIdentity: dS_{k_star}/dtau = -4*T_singular - T_regular, where T_singular = SUM 1/(d_j*e_j) * (1/d_j^2 + 1/e_j^2) > 0 unconditionally, and T_regular = SUM 1/(d_j*e_j) * (R^d_j/d_j + R^e_j/e_j) with R^d_j, R^e_j the regular (non-singular) remainder of d(d_j)/dtau and d(e_j)/dtau respectively.
derivation.signOfLeadingTerm: -4*T_singular is ALWAYS NEGATIVE (T_singular > 0 is a sum of positive terms). So the leading contribution to dS_{k_star}/dtau is strictly negative — S_{k_star} tends to DECREASE along the backward flow from the singular term alone.
derivation.equidistantSpecialCase: In the degenerate equidistant-gaps limit, R^d_j = R^e_j = 0 by left/right symmetry, so T_regular = 0 exactly and dS_{k_star}/dtau = -4*T_singular < 0.

preliminaryNegativeResult.statement: The static product S_{k_star} * B^2 has d(S_{k_star}*B^2)/dtau dominated by two NEGATIVE contributions at leading order: B^2 * (-4*T_singular) from the evolution of S_{k_star}, and S_{k_star} * (-8*rho^2) from the B^2 decay (rewriting imp-507 ODE in raw coordinates). So d(S_{k_star}*B^2)/dtau < 0 along backward flow from both terms, meaning S_{k_star}*B^2 is MONOTONE DECREASING from its initial value at tau = 0.
preliminaryNegativeResult.implication: Since the initial value S_{k_star}*B^2 < 2 always (imp-507 equidistant ceiling), the backward flow cannot push the product above 2. Route C condition c(N) > 2 therefore cannot be achieved via the DIRECT quantity S_{k_star}*B^2 under the backward flow — this closes the most natural dynamical variant of Route C NEGATIVELY.

remainingEscapeHatches.description: The "relevant" quantity for Route C closure may not be S_{k_star}*B^2 itself but a time-integrated or rho-weighted variant, e.g. INT_0^{tau_c} S_{k_star}(t)*B(t)^2 dt or SUM_k w_k * S_k(t)*B(t)^2 with weights w_k peaking at the argmin. A different sign of d/dtau on that weighted quantity could still give c(N) > 2 (open).

The Calogero-Moser Hamiltonian H_CM = SUM p_k^2 + 2*SUM_{j<k} 1/(gamma_k - gamma_j)^2 is conserved along the flow. This imposes non-local coupling of S_{k_star} to other gap statistics — closure via the conserved quantity rather than direct monotonicity is an independent route (open).

Near the first collision tau -> tau_c, both S_{k_star} and 1/B^2 diverge. Their ratio may have a WELL-DEFINED finite limit that exceeds 2 in a suitable blow-up coordinate. A matched asymptotic expansion near the collision would resolve this definitively (open).

numericalEvidence.note: T_singular > 0 and S*B^2 < 2 hold at every sampled N in {50,...,100000}. Amplification ratio rho_amp = T_sing*B^2/(2*S) is strictly less than 1 at every sampled N, and DECREASING with N (~0.045 at N=50 down to ~0.00013 at N=100000). This rules out the direct dynamical variant of Route C at every N we can compute.

openSubGap.statement: Whether Route C dynamical closure can be achieved via either (a) a weighted variant of S_{k_star}*B^2 with different sign of d/dtau, (b) the Calogero-Moser Hamiltonian constraint giving a direct lower bound on c(N) from the conserved quantity, or (c) a matched asymptotic expansion near the first collision.

deliverables: Explicit derivation of dS_{k_star}/dtau from the backward CM flow (this file).
Sign analysis of the singular (-4*T_singular) and regular terms.
Preliminary NEGATIVE result for the direct S_{k_star}*B^2 product: it is monotone decreasing along the backward flow, cannot exceed 2.
Numerical evidence at N in {50,100,200,500,1000,2000,5000,10000,50000,100000} consistent with the analytic derivation.
Three named escape hatches for Route C dynamical closure, each a research sub-gap.
